title: I think it's coming along. Some gameplay finally.
author: bahaw1024
selftext:
Does it look like a real game? how does it look? any feedback is welcome. 

I utilized a lot of AI in the process to learn about AI mostly with Claude. Experimenting with token usage, skills, proven pipelines that are fully automated. I think most of the process besides playtest is automated now. I would love to share my knowledge if anyone is struggling with assets or anything. Not saying i have it all figured out either lol

comments.author: Outrageous_Fix173
comments.body: looks cool, what was pipeline for UI? is it assets or generated?

replies.author: bahaw1024
replies.body:
so sorry about the reply...  
  
Crap, i read your question wrong and wrote all that below but you are asking about UI. I asked claude to give me 3-4 design options based on a theme. I planned out a theme beforehand then stuck to it then each time i wanted to work on UI, I would ask for 3-4 designs and then choose what i like, fine tune it. and then asked it to dcoument the process and flow and asked to do each section of UI bit my bit. for example notification center was its own work, then the objectives panel, the HUD on the right. the msuic player such.   


Sure, there was another post about this in a claude related sub but I forget where that was doing something  similar. Here is what worked for me; 

I generated prompts using claude for assets/characters (whatever i needed, env props, anything ) I kept a style/guide for my game saved so i dont deviate the prompts from the style ( I worked on this separately) So everytime claude generates a prompt, its based on that style. I fed that prompt to chatgpt, It's better at these kind of images and faster , imo and experience. then i take the image and feed it into [meshy.ai](http://meshy.ai) or tripo. i stopped meshy and went to tripo recently and found more luck. but in the beginning i used free assets too btw so if you dont want to spend money. PLUS BLENDER HAS A MCP so if you're art style is 2d or pixel or somethign easier for AI then it can be free. Once i get the model from from tripo/meshy, i download and upload to mixamo to rig for animation (mixamo has free animation), then download again. i repeat the process for however many characters and then props dont need animation so its all there.

comments.author: EntertainmentNew1789
comments.body:
holy crap. How do you keep the context from turning into a mess after a long back-and-forth with Claude? And how do you stop it from forgetting stuff or quietly changing things?  
this is the demo I’ve been dreaming of making -.-

replies.author: bahaw1024
replies.body:
I do a few things that have helped me personally. 

1. I didn’t use full auto mode or anything else until this had a good set of rules or memories written (stuff like remember to give me smaller responses, never purchase anything without explicit permission and a bunch of small things like no code file should be more than 500 lines blah  blah

2. Each feature or bug it’s usually its own chat. Unless I m bug smashing and logging bugs then that’s a chat in it self but in that chat I m just logging and grooming bugs. 

3. I added a lot of testing but careful running too many tests all the time. 

4. If you are having a long back forth, then you can manually /compact info when you feel like you are not getting the results you want.

replies.author: EntertainmentNew1789
replies.body: 2 and 4 really clicked for me, thanks. Also, are the art assets in the demo already wired into the engine?
